# Data Model Comparison

Dimension comparing Notion's block/database model with Obsidian's plain markdown
files. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Notion's Data Model

### Block Model

Every piece of content — text, heading, image, embed, database row, even a page
itself — is a block with a UUID v4 identifier, type, properties, and
parent/child relationships [2]. Data is stored server-side in PostgreSQL, sharded
across 480 logical shards [15]. Users do not have direct filesystem access.

### Databases

Notion databases support 8 view types and 19+ property types [16]:

**View types:** Table, Board (Kanban), Timeline (Gantt), Calendar, List, Gallery,
Chart (column/line/pie), Form [16].

**Property types (14 writable):** Text, Number, Select, Multi-Select, Status,
Date, Person, Files & Media, Checkbox, URL, Email, Phone, Relation, Owner [16].

**Property types (9 read-only):** Formula, Rollup, Created time, Created by,
Last edited time, Last edited by, Button, ID, Verification [16].

**Advanced features:** Relations (cross-database linking), Rollups (aggregate
related data), Formulas (custom calculations), Linked Databases (filtered views
elsewhere), "Load Limit" pagination [16].

## Obsidian's Data Model

Obsidian stores notes as plain `.md` files on the user's local filesystem. The
"vault" is a folder of markdown files. There is no server-side database, no
block UUID system, no proprietary format. Markdown is the canonical data format,
not a secondary export path.

For detailed Obsidian architecture, see the existing research at
[research/obsidian-pa-integration/](../../obsidian-pa-integration/).

## Comparison Table

| Dimension | Notion | Obsidian |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Storage location | Cloud (Notion servers, PostgreSQL) [15] | Local filesystem |
| Data format | Proprietary block model [2] | Plain markdown (.md) |
| Unit of content | Block (UUID v4) [2] | File |
| Databases | 8 views, 19+ properties, relations [16] | Dataview plugin queries frontmatter |
| Knowledge graph | No native graph view | Core feature (global + local) |
| Linking | Automated backlinks, paragraph-level [17] | Wiki-style `[[links]]`, bi-directional |
| Export | PDF, HTML, Markdown/CSV (lossy) [5] | N/A — files are already portable |
| Round-trip fidelity | "You can't instantly recreate your workspace" [5] | Native — files are the source |
| Vendor lock-in risk | Moderate-high (rich features lost on export) | Low (standard file format) |

## Markdown Support

Notion's markdown handling is inconsistent [14]:

- **Fully supported:** Headings, bold, italic, lists, code blocks, task lists,
  emoji, auto URL linking
- **Partially supported:** Links, images, and tables work via copy-paste but
  "you can't type them in Notion's editor" [14] — must use slash commands
- **Unsupported:** Footnotes, heading IDs, definition lists, highlight,
  subscript, superscript [14]

Obsidian is markdown-native. It supports standard markdown plus extensions
(footnotes, callouts, Mermaid diagrams, LaTeX math) via core features and
plugins. Markdown is the source format, not a conversion target.

## Export and Import

### Notion Export [5]

- **Formats:** PDF, HTML, Markdown & CSV
- **Includes:** Pages, subpages (Business/Enterprise toggle), images, comments
  (HTML only), workspace-level export with sitemap
- **Limitations:** Form views cannot be exported; only current database view
  exports; custom emojis lost in PDF; Windows 260-char path limit; 7-day
  download link expiration; owners can disable exports

### Notion Import [11]

- **Formats:** .txt, .md, .docx, .csv, .html, .pdf, .zip
- **App integrations:** Evernote, Trello, Google Docs, Quip, Dropbox Paper,
  Hackpad, WorkFlowy, Confluence, Asana, Monday.com
- **File caps:** Free 5MB, Paid 50MB (docs/HTML) / 20MB (PDF) [11]
- **Volume:** ~5,000 items for Evernote/Trello, 5GB / ~10,000 files for ZIP,
  ~120 imports per 12 hours [11]

### Obsidian

No import/export needed — files are standard markdown on disk. Any markdown
editor can read them. Migration to/from other tools is a file copy operation.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Obsidian data model claims in this document are general knowledge, not
  sourced from fetched URLs. See [obsidian-pa-integration](../../obsidian-pa-integration/)
  for cited Obsidian details.
- Notion database performance characteristics (row limits, query speed) are
  not well-documented in official sources
- The "Load Limit" pagination setting [16] suggests performance management
  but hard limits are not published
